action_access_logs_desc: Browse the ship's logs and crew manifests stored on the terminal.
action_assemble_comms_desc: Put the repaired parts together — replace the amplifier, insert the power cell, straighten the connector.
action_assess_supplies_desc: Take stock of the cafeteria's remaining food and water reserves.
action_check_bridge_terminal_desc: Attempt to log in to the engineering terminal on the bridge.
action_check_comms_desc: Access the comms station and scan for signals or distress calls.
action_check_navigation_desc: Power up the navigation console and determine your current position.
action_check_reactor_status_desc: Run a detailed diagnostic of the ship's reactor and power systems.
action_check_status_desc: Check the overall status of the ship.
action_check_storage_desc: Search the storage locker for emergency supplies.
action_check_terminal_desc: Try to log into the terminal. From there you should be able to disable that annoying alarm and maybe figure out why it went off.
action_debug_taxing_desc: 10-second taxing action to test resource drains.
action_disable_alarm_desc: Access the terminal overrides and disable the blaring emergency alarm.
action_drink_water_desc: Drink the water that's left in the broken recycler. Not clean, but it'll quench your thirst.
action_enter_known_credentials_bridge_de: Try the credentials you found in the crew quarters on the bridge terminal.
action_enter_known_credentials_desc: Try the credentials you found on the bridge on the crew quarters terminal.
action_enter_known_credentials_name_desc: Log into the terminal using credentials you already know.
action_extract_rover_fuel_cell_desc: Open the rover's service panel and carefully remove the high-capacity fuel cell. This will take both skill and strength.
action_fabricate_amplifier_desc: Use the fabricator to produce a new signal amplifier.
action_fabricate_parts_desc: Use the fabricator to synthesize replacement components from raw stock.
action_go_crew_quarters_desc: Head back to the crew quarters.
action_go_to_crew_quarters_desc: Head back to the crew quarters.
action_go_to_main_area_desc: Head to the main gathering area and cafeteria.
action_go_workshop_desc: Head to the maintenance workshop to check supplies and equipment.
action_grab_bottled_water_desc: Snatch a sealed bottle of water from the cafeteria supplies.
action_grab_login_note_desc: Take the found sticky note with terminal login credentials.
action_grab_proviant_desc: Grab a few remaining ration packs from the cafeteria. There isn't much left.
action_grab_tools_desc: Take a basic set of repair tools from the workshop.
action_grab_uniform_desc: Your SFC flight uniform hangs on the wall by your bunk. Integrated oxygen system, hermetic seals — full survival kit.
action_hack_bridge_terminal_desc: Attempt to brute-force the bridge engineering terminal.
action_hack_terminal_desc: Spend time bypassing the terminal's security. A long, focused task that will eventually grant full access.
action_inspect_bikes_desc: Take a look at the two folding scout bikes leaning against the wall.
action_inspect_rover_desc: Examine the scout rover parked on the lift ramp.
action_inspect_workshop_terminal_desc: Check out the terminal in the corner of the room.
action_install_comms_desc: Slot the repaired panel back into the communications station.
action_install_rover_fuel_cell_desc: Connect the rover's fuel cell directly to the ship's main reactor. Thanks to the schematics from the workshop, you know exactly how.
action_investigate_desc: Spend energy to study the loop signature and learn from it.
action_learn_fabricator_desc: Study the control panel and manual of the fabricator.
action_listen_for_response_desc: Tune in and wait for a response to the distress signal.
action_optimize_reactor_desc: Shut down non-essential systems and reconfigure power distribution to reduce fuel consumption. Requires terminal access.
action_optimize_reactor_remote_desc: You already know the reactor is dying. Through the terminal in your quarters you can run the optimization — you know the right parameters by heart.
action_read_book_desc: Study the repair manual you found under your pillow. Learn basic scout ship maintenance procedures.
action_read_vehicle_manual_desc: Read the "Off-Road Vehicle Maintenance for Space Castaways" manual.
action_remove_engine_panel_desc: Take off the access panel to the main reactor. Heavy metal plates, but with the right tools it'll come off.
action_repair_kit_desc: Attempt to repair damaged equipment found in the workshop.
action_repair_recycler_desc: The water recycler in the cafeteria is broken. If you could fix it, it might replenish the water supply.
action_repair_ship_systems_desc: Run diagnostics and patch damaged systems from the workbench. A taxing but rewarding task.
action_rest_desc: Take a brief rest to recover stamina.
action_scan_desc: Analyze incoming anomalies and gain experience.
action_scan_gamma_site_desc: The comms panel gave you an approximate fix, but the search radius is still too wide for navigation. The ship's scanner, however, can lock onto the exact target — now that it knows where to point.
action_scan_planet_surface_desc: Prep a probe and have it perform a detailed surface scan. Sensor calibration requires maximum focus — every parameter must be precise.
action_scavenge_tools_desc: Search the workshop for usable tools and components.
action_search_bunks_desc: Search your bunk and the surrounding area — maybe something useful can be found.
action_search_for_login_note_desc: Search the workbench area for a sticky note with terminal login credentials.
action_search_workbench_desc: Search the workshop workbench — maybe something useful can be found.
action_send_distress_signal_desc: Record a message and broadcast a call for help.
action_send_ping_desc: Send a signal into the surroundings.
action_set_course_gamma_desc: Enter Gamma Site coordinates into the navigation system and set a course for the research station.
action_stabilize_desc: Use supplies to keep the loop from fragmenting.
action_study_ship_manual_desc: Browse the technical schematics and documentation for the Vagabond-class scout ship on the workshop terminal. The power system specs must be in here somewhere.
action_survey_area_desc: Carefully examine the workshop layout for hidden caches.
action_tinker_device_desc: Examine the half-finished gadget on the prototype bench. You have no idea what it does, but it looks like it has a working power cell inside.
action_use_bridge_terminal_login_desc: Use found credentials to access the bridge terminal.
action_use_terminal_login_desc: Use the found login credentials to access the terminal immediately.
action_wake_up_desc: Shake off the grogginess and climb out of the bunk. Time to assess the situation.
log_gamma_route_no_fuel: The journey to Gamma Site has halted — fuel reserves are depleted. Without power, Vagabond cannot continue the flight.
log_gamma_route_rover_hint: There might be a rover in the garage with a usable fuel cell. If you can extract and install it, you could get enough fuel to complete the journey.
log_gamma_route_resumed: Fuel restored — Vagabond resumes course toward Gamma Site.
obj_disable_alarm_narrative: The terminal is locked behind a login screen. You could try to hack it — you know your way around this system, but it will take a while. Or search the ship — you noticed a sticky note on the monitor that says "workshop". Maybe someone left credentials there.\n\nOnce you have access, shut down that blaring alarm before it drives you insane.
obj_disable_alarm_step2: Gain access (hack or log in with credentials)
obj_establish_contact_narrative: The communications system is damaged, but might be salvageable. If you can send out a signal, you might pick up a response from other survivors.
obj_reactor_status_narrative: The ship reactor is in an unknown state. If it fails, the ship loses all power. Get to the bridge and check on the reactor — it may need repairs or optimization.
obj_reactor_status_step2b: Gain terminal access (hack or find login)
obj_repair_recycler_narrative: Drinking water supplies are critically low. The water recycler has a damaged filter — without repairs, water will run out in a few days. You need tools and knowledge to fix it.
obj_repair_recycler_step1: Assess supplies in the main area
obj_rover_fuel_narrative: While inspecting the rover, you discovered an intact fuel cell. If you can extract it and connect it to the main reactor, the ship will gain precious extra energy. It will require tools, knowledge, and access to the engine room.
obj_reach_gamma_site_narrative: You've intercepted a signal and extracted coordinates for Gamma Site — a research station somewhere on the planet below. Someone — or something — called out from there. Get to the bridge, lock in the coordinates, and chart a course.
obj_reach_gamma_step2: Gain access to the bridge terminal
obj_reach_gamma_step3: Confirm Gamma Site location on the scanner
obj_reach_gamma_step5: Survive the journey to Gamma Site
obj_survive_narrative:
You did it. Against all odds, the Vagabond is yours — a stolen scout ship carrying you away from Katarnis VII and a lifetime of unjust labor. But freedom has come at a steep price.

The ship is barely holding together. Systems are failing, navigation data is wiped, and you lack the training to fix any of it. Somewhere in the blackness ahead, a gravitational anomaly tugs at the hull — as if something has been waiting.

Your first priority is simple: get your bearings and survive the next hour.
obj_survive_narrative_loop1: You woke up with a strange feeling — as if you have lived through all of this before. Just a bad dream? Or is something wrong with your memory? The ship is still falling apart, but you... you feel like you already know what to do.
obj_survive_narrative_loop2: You know now. This is not the first time. A time loop — you wake up at the same moment, with the same problems. But your memories remain. Now it is about using every minute better than last time.
obj_survive_step1: Wake up and get your bearings
obj_survive_step2: Gain access to the ship terminal
result_access_logs: You access the ship's logs. Most records are corrupted, but fragments remain: coordinates, crew assignments, and a cryptic reference to 'Gamma Site' on the planet below.
result_assemble_comms: The last component clicks into place. The panel's indicator blinks — for the first time since the crash. You're holding a functional comms unit. The very device you destroyed to escape. The irony is not lost on you.
result_assemble_comms_known: Your hands remember every step. In moments the panel is assembled — routine.
result_assess_supplies: You take stock of the cafeteria supplies. Food has almost completely run out — barely a few ration packs remain. The water recycler is dead. In the fridge, however, you find two sealed bottles of clean water. At least something.
result_check_bridge_terminal: You tap the engineering console. The screen flickers to the ship system login screen. Without credentials you can't proceed. Maybe you could try hacking it.
result_check_bridge_terminal_first_has_l: You tap the engineering console. The login screen looks familiar — same system as the crew quarters terminal. The password you already have might work here too.
result_check_bridge_terminal_known: You tap the console. You enter the credentials with confidence — you know them by now. The system lets you in with a soft chime.
result_check_bridge_terminal_loop1: You tap the console… and freeze. Your fingers move before your mind catches up — you already know the password. You don't know how you know. A chill runs through you. Better just type it in.
result_check_bridge_terminal_loop2: You don't even hesitate. The password is already beneath your fingertips — you've done this so many times it's automatic. All that's left is to type it in.
result_check_comms: You power up the comms station. Static fills most channels, but a faint beacon repeats on loop — a pre-recorded distress signal from the ship itself.
result_check_comms_loop2: You power up the station. The panel is here — as if nothing happened. But you know you ripped it out yesterday... or was that just a dream? No — you remember the damage exactly. Missing power cell, fried amplifier, bent connector. Dream or not, you know what to do.
result_check_comms_loop3: You power up the station. You're not even surprised the panel is back anymore. You're not surprised by anything. You know what it is and what to do with it.
result_check_comms_v2: You power up the station. Nothing but static. The panel is gone — just bare wires where the comms module should be. During your escape, you tore it from the console and threw it on the ground so they couldn't track you. You give it a quick inspection: fried signal amplifier, missing power cell, bent connector. You'll need the fabricator for a new amplifier, a power cell, and proper tools. You should be able to find that in the workshop.
result_check_navigation_coords: Navigation systems confirm your position. Gamma Site is directly below — the coordinates match down to the meter. All that's left now is to set a course.
result_check_navigation_first: The navigation console flickers to life after a brief struggle. According to the data, there's a planet within the ship's sensor range. Initial estimates suggest it could theoretically be habitable — similar temperature, signs of an atmosphere... But honestly, you've passed dozens of planets like this on your journey. Nothing special. For peace of mind, you could prep a probe and have it scan the surface for anomalies.
result_check_navigation_known: You approach the navigation console and a memory surfaces — you've done this before. That planet below? Empty. You spent hours calibrating the probe just for it to tell you what you already suspected. No anomalies, unbreathable atmosphere. A waste of time. You're not wasting another probe on that.
result_check_navigation_loop: You approach the navigation console and a strange feeling washes over you — like you already know exactly what you'll see. That planet... have you scanned it before? Or was it just a dream? Something tells you launching a probe would be a waste of time. But you're not certain.
result_check_ping_results_first: You access the comms console and analyze the incoming data. The signal is faint and fragmented — you can only lock onto a partial set of coordinates. It appears to be the Gamma Site research station, but you'll need to send a targeted ping to pinpoint the exact location.
result_check_ping_results_targeted: The console beeps — the targeted ping has returned. You lean in as the data resolves on screen: Gamma Site Research Station, exact coordinates locked. This is it — a real destination. Somewhere down there, something has been waiting. You need to get to the bridge navigation system and set a course.
result_check_reactor_status: The reactor scan reveals critical fuel depletion — only {fuel} units remain. At current burn rate you have roughly {minutes} minutes before the reactor goes cold. Without power, life support will fail and oxygen reserves will drain rapidly.
result_check_reactor_status_known: Just like in that dream… was it ever a dream? Everything is exactly the same — the readings, the fuel gauge, the sinking feeling in your chest. This isn't possible. And yet here you are, staring at the same numbers. You have {minutes} minutes before the reactor dies. Again.
result_check_reactor_status_loop2: Unfortunately your prediction came true, the fuel status is exactly what you thought. {fuel} units of fuel, {minutes} minutes until darkness. You knew it before you even got out of bed.
result_check_status: Overall ship status: CRITICAL. Multiple systems are failing, but the core structure is intact. You have time, but not much.
result_check_storage: The storage locker contains emergency rations, a med-kit, a portable scanner, and an empty canteen. Standard issue for exploration missions.
result_check_storage_loop1: Maybe it was a dream, but you've searched this locker before. And the canteen was there — empty, ready for use. You take it.
result_check_storage_loop2: Exactly as you remember — an empty canteen lies in the storage locker. You grab it without hesitation.
result_check_terminal: You tap the console and the screen flickers to life, demanding credentials. You tried a few random passwords but no luck. Fortunately, you have some experience with this operating system and should be able to hack into the terminal — it'll just take a while. Oh, and you noticed a sticky note on the monitor — "workshop". Maybe the login can be found there?
result_check_terminal_first_has_login: You tap the console. The login screen looks familiar — same system as the bridge terminal. The password you already have might work here too.
result_check_terminal_known: You tap the console. You already know the password — you type it in with confidence. The screen dissolves with a soft chime. You're in.
result_check_terminal_loop1: You tap the console… and freeze. Your fingers move before your mind catches up — you already know the password. You don't know how you know. A chill runs through you. Better just type it in.
result_check_terminal_loop2: You don't even hesitate. The password is already beneath your fingertips — you've done this so many times the routine is automatic. All that's left is to type it in.
result_disable_alarm: You key in the override codes. The wailing alarm sputters and dies. Blessed silence fills the compartment. The ringing in your ears will fade — eventually.
result_enter_known_credentials: You enter the known password and the screen dissolves with a soft chime. You're in.
result_enter_known_credentials_bridge: You enter the credentials from the crew quarters. They work. The system lets you in.
result_enter_known_credentials_bridge_lo: You type the credentials from memory. Routine at this point. The system lets you in.
result_enter_known_credentials_loop2: You type in the password without thinking. It's become muscle memory at this point. The screen dissolves with a soft chime. You're in.
result_extract_rover_fuel_cell: After wrestling with the service panel and a few stubborn bolts, you manage to extract the fuel cell. It's heavier than it looks — and still charged. Could serve as an emergency power source for the ship.
result_extract_rover_fuel_cell_known: You know the drill — a few quick moves and the fuel cell is out.
result_extract_rover_fuel_cell_loop2: Routine. Service panel, bolts, cell out. You don't even break a sweat.
result_fabricate_amplifier: You enter parameters into the fabricator. First attempt fails — the amplifier won't pass calibration. Second one too. Eventually, after painstaking adjustments, you find the right configuration. The fabricator hums and ejects a clean, functional amplifier.
result_fabricate_amplifier_book: Thanks to the repair manual, you know exactly what parameters to enter. The fabricator whirs and soon ejects a clean, functional amplifier.
result_fabricate_amplifier_known: Your fingers automatically tap in the correct sequence. The fabricator barely has time to spin up before spitting out a finished part.
result_fabricate_parts: The fabricator whirs to life, layering polymer and alloy into precise shapes. A tray of fresh components slides out — exactly what you'd need for field repairs.
result_go_to_bridge: You head to the ship's bridge.
result_go_to_crew_quarters: You return to the crew quarters.
result_go_to_main_area: You head to the main area.
result_grab_bottled_water: You grab a sealed bottle of water from the cafeteria counter. Clean and cool — it will come in handy.
result_grab_login_note: You take the sticky note. "terminal — user: crew01 / pass: vagabond47". This could come in handy.
result_grab_tools: You rummage through the workbench and find a set of repair tools. Exactly what you needed.
result_grab_uniform: You put on the suit with its own small oxygen supply. It buys you precious extra time.
result_grab_uniform_loop1: Last time you didn't bother — it seemed pointless. But now you've got a weird feeling... like you know what's coming. Better grab it right away. You click the hermetic seals and the system beeps quietly.
result_grab_uniform_loop2: You know exactly what awaits. The uniform goes on automatically — pure routine. In seconds you're suited up and ready.
result_grab_uniform_tried: Suddenly the heat and restricted movement don't bother you so much — what matters is you'll have a chance to breathe. You put on the suit with its own small oxygen supply. It buys you precious extra time.
result_hack_bridge_terminal: After painstaking trial and error, you finally crack the engineering terminal's authentication. The system welcomes you with a soft chime — and you won't forget the login now.
result_hack_terminal: After painstaking trial and error, you finally crack the terminal's authentication. The system welcomes you with a soft chime. You're in — and you won't forget the login now.
result_inspect_bikes_loop1: Still no fuel, still no juice. But last time you realized they're not total junk — the engines are in good shape.
result_inspect_bikes_loop2: Empty tanks, dead batteries. Nothing new.
result_inspect_bikes_skilled: Tanks are dry, batteries dead — useless without fuel and a charge. But the engines themselves look functional.
result_inspect_rover_loop1: You've seen this before. Last time it occurred to you that the fuel cell might not be junk. What if it really wasn't just a dream?
result_inspect_rover_loop2: Same wreck. Dented frame, dead battery — but the fuel cell is still there, partially drained but undamaged.
result_inspect_rover_skilled: The rover is in terrible shape — dead battery, cracked hose, dented frame. But the fuel cell looks undamaged — maybe it could still be useful?
result_inspect_workshop_terminal: The terminal is unlocked — no password required. It offers several manuals to browse.
result_inspect_workshop_terminal_loop1: The terminal is unlocked. It offers the same manuals as before — nothing new.
result_install_comms: You slide the panel into the console. For a second, nothing... then the screen lights up. No static. A clean signal. The ship's communications system is alive.
result_install_rover_fuel_cell: With bated breath you plug in the last connector. A quiet hum fills the air as the reactor draws energy from the cell. The dashboard shows a gain of 300 units — the ship now has more fuel than before.
result_install_rover_fuel_cell_known: You've done this before. The cell slots into place like it belongs there — +300 fuel.
result_install_rover_fuel_cell_loop2: The connectors click on the first try. The ship gratefully welcomes its fuel boost.
result_learn_fabricator: You flip through the available menus — metal sheets, polymer parts, circuits. This machine can make almost anything... but you have no idea what you should even try.
result_learn_fabricator_hint: Now you understand how the fabricator works. And it hits you — that comms panel from the main area! It needs exactly this kind of amplifier. If only you had the right parameters...
log_ping_response_ready: A beeping sound comes from the comms console — the ping has returned. You should check the results.
effect_on_route_gamma_desc: Vagabond is heading toward the Gamma Site research station. The nav computer is counting down to arrival.
result_listen_for_response_loop2: Hours of waiting. And then — for a second, maybe two — something breaks through the static. Not a voice, more like... the impression of a voice. Like hearing your own name in the wind. One word, perhaps: 'Gamma'? Or did you imagine it? You're exhausted. Maybe you're hearing things. But somewhere deep down, you feel it wasn't just your head.
result_listen_for_response_loop3: This time you're ready. You wait. And it comes — faint but unmistakable, a voice cutting through the static: '...Gamma Site Research... evacuation failed... anomaly...' The message fragments. But it's no longer an illusion. Someone down there was there — and they warned.
result_listen_for_response_loop4: Right at the exact moment you amplify the signal. The voice is clearer: '...Gamma Site Research Station, sector 7-Gamma. Repeating coordinates: 47.3—' Static. Then again: '...temporal anomaly active. Gamma Site ending transmission.' Now you know everything. Where it is. And that something is waiting for you there.
result_optimize_reactor: You sit at the engineering console and scroll through the list of active systems. Section by section, you shut down everything that isn't absolutely critical — cabin heating for empty quarters, backup comms arrays, lab equipment. Fuel consumption drops visibly. You've bought precious extra time.
result_optimize_reactor_known: You know exactly what to look for. In seconds you flip the necessary switches. Fuel consumption drops once again.
result_optimize_reactor_remote: You flip through familiar configuration panels, shutting down everything non-essential. Fuel consumption drops visibly — you've bought precious extra time.
result_read_book: You turn the final page and close the book. You've picked up some basic repair techniques. Maybe you could handle small fixes now.
result_read_vehicle_manual: You turn the last page. The manual was written for complete idiots — perfect. You now understand off-road vehicle drive basics, fault diagnostics, and most importantly: how the fuel system on SFC-class rovers works.
result_remove_engine_panel: A few sweaty minutes and the panel is down. The guts of the engine room open up before you — the main reactor hums quietly, but you can clearly see the connection point for an external source. You have no idea how to wire it up though... a memory flickers — technical schematics stored on the workshop terminal.
result_remove_engine_panel_known: You know this panel by heart — off in seconds.
result_repair_kit: Using the salvaged components you manage to repair a damaged enviro-suit. It's not perfect, but it will hold for now.
result_repair_recycler_first: After twenty minutes of tinkering inside the machine, a quiet hum finally starts. Water begins to drip from the spout — slowly at first, then a steady stream. The recycler is working again.
result_repair_recycler_remember: Familiar routine. Your hands remember every step. In half the time, the recycler is back online.
result_repair_ship_systems: You spend several minutes elbow-deep in wiring harnesses and circuit boards. Several warning indicators flicker from red to amber. Not fixed — but improved.
result_scan_gamma_site: You enter the precise coordinates of Gamma Site. The probe locks onto a single point on the surface — and the results are immediate. A research station. It's there. Damaged, abandoned, but still standing. And the sensors detect a faint energy signature — something down there is still operational.
result_scan_planet_surface: The probe completes its scan. The results are... unremarkable. No signs of civilization, no anomalies. The atmosphere is barely suitable for humans — high CO₂, low oxygen. This won't be your new home. Further scanning would just be a waste of time.
result_scavenge_tools: You scour the workshop. Several toolkits are still intact. You salvage what you can — a plasma cutter and some spare power cells.
result_search_bunks: You rummage through the bunk. Beneath the pillow, your fingers brush against something unexpected — a worn repair manual. 'Scout Ship Maintenance for Complete Idiots.' Someone from the crew must have left it here. This could come in handy.
result_search_bunks_bookread: You search the bunk. The manual is still there, but you've already read it — nothing new to learn.
result_search_bunks_loop1: You search the bunk. You had an odd feeling something would be there — and sure enough, beneath the pillow you find the same worn manual. Was it just a dream, or…?
result_search_bunks_loop2: You reach under the pillow with certainty. The repair manual. Exactly as you remembered.
result_search_for_login_note: You rummage through the clutter on the workbench. Tucked under a coffee-stained schematic, you find a sticky note: "terminal — user: crew01 / pass: vagabond47". This could be useful back at terminal.
result_search_workbench: You rummage through the clutter on the workbench. Under a coffee-stained schematic you find a sticky note with login credentials. In the drawer you also discover a set of repair tools — exactly what you might need.
result_send_distress_signal: You record the message. 'This is SFC-47 Vagabond. Emergency situation. Requesting assistance.' Signal sent. Minutes tick by. No response comes. The reactor dies first — you didn't make it. Next time, this has to be your absolute top priority. Send the signal as soon as possible, and hope.
result_send_targeted_ping_loop: You remember the approximate location of the signal from the previous loop. You aim the antenna exactly where it needs to go — targeted ping sent.
result_set_course_gamma: You enter the coordinates. The nav computer thinks for a moment, then blinks confirmation. Vagabond alters course. Gamma Site. Whatever waits down there — you're heading toward it.
result_study_ship_manual: You spend an hour poring over schematic after schematic. Finally you find the power section — including a diagram for connecting an external source to the main reactor. Now you know exactly how to wire up that fuel cell.
result_tinker_device: You have no idea what this device is for — a mess of wires, lenses and circuits. But one thing's clear: there's a functional power cell inside. With the help of your tools, you manage to pry it out without destroying the rest.
result_tinker_device_known: You know exactly where to reach. A few clicks and the power cell is out.
result_use_bridge_terminal_login: You enter the credentials from the sticky note into the engineering console. The lock screen dissolves instantly. You're in.
result_use_terminal_login: You enter the credentials from the sticky note. The lock screen dissolves instantly. You're in — terminal access granted.
result_wake_up: You push yourself up, body aching. You are alive and the ship is still intact — barely. However just as you put your feet on the ground from the bed a loud red alert started howling across the ship, time to check what is happening.
result_wake_up_loop1: You push yourself up, body aching... but something feels off. The alarm — it started at exactly the same moment, just as your feet touched the floor. A strange sense of familiarity you can't explain. You shake it off. Time to figure out what happened.
result_wake_up_loop2: You bolt upright, heart racing before the alarm even sounds — and right on cue, it blares. Exactly when you expected. This can't be coincidence. The same ship. The same moment. If this day is repeating itself, you realize the reactor died at the exact same instant every time. If I'm truly trapped in some kind of time loop, I have exactly {minutes} minutes before it happens again. I'll have to figure out a solution or go insane.
result_wake_up_loop3: You bolt upright. There's no point in checking the fuel status anymore, you know exactly how it looks. {fuel} units of fuel, {minutes} minutes until the reactor dies. Every time the same. Every time the same end.
